key_insight: Introduce an explicit self-awareness module that models the agent's pose, observations, and explored map and fuses this with a Vision-Language Model so the agent can both reason about instructions and explain its navigation decisions.
problem_solved: VLN agents often either rely on opaque end-to-end VLM reasoning or brittle hand-crafted maps; this work tackles the gap by combining explicit, interpretable agent-centric mapping with VLM reasoning to improve grounded, explainable action selection.
method: Construct an agent-centric self-awareness representation capturing pose, observed landmarks, and explored free/blocked regions as an explicit scene map.
Fuse the explicit map and agent state with a Vision-Language Model so instruction grounding, scene understanding, and action prediction happen jointly but remain interpretable.
Use the combined representation to guide a planner that selects actions and emits human-readable rationale for decisions (hybrid map-based planning + VLM reasoning).
impact: Provides a practical middle ground between black-box VLM policies and rigid map planners, enabling more reliable, interpretable VLN agents—useful for robotics, embodied AI research, and systems requiring traceable decisions.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: self-awareness module (map + state) feeding into a VLM and planner, with arrows showing information flow.
Step-by-step example: instruction → panorama snapshots + local map updates → chosen action with short rationale.
Map overlay: explored map showing trajectory, visited landmarks, and predicted next actions to highlight interpretability.
Comparison panel: qualitative side-by-side of black-box VLM vs AwareVLN explanations (why an action was chosen).
paper_title: AwareVLN: Reasoning with Self-awareness for Vision-Language Navigation
paper_authors: Wenxuan Guo, Xiuwei Xu, Yichen Liu, Xiangyu Li, Hang Yin
